statement.p: Let A=\left[\begin{matrix} 4 \amp 2 \amp 18 \cr 3 \amp 2 \amp 14 \cr \end{matrix}\right], {\bf b}=\left[\begin{matrix} -4 \cr -1 \cr 1 \cr \end{matrix}\right], and {\bf c}=\left[\begin{matrix} 10 \cr 9 \cr \end{matrix}\right]. Define T({\bf x})=A{\bf x}.
Select true or false for each statement.

li.p: The vector {\bf c} is in the range of T
The vector {\bf b} is in the kernel of T

static.solution:
A{\bf b}=\left[\begin{matrix} 4 \amp 2 \amp 18 \cr 3 \amp 2 \amp 14 \cr \end{matrix}\right] \left[\begin{matrix} -4 \cr -1 \cr 1 \cr \end{matrix}\right]= \left[\begin{matrix} 0 \cr 0 \cr \end{matrix}\right], so {\bf b}\in \ker(T).
We row-reduce to determine a solution of A{\bf x}={\bf c}.
\left[\begin{matrix} 4 \amp 2 \amp 18 \amp 10 \cr 3 \amp 2 \amp 14 \amp 9 \cr \end{matrix}\right]\sim \left[\begin{matrix} 1 \amp 0 \amp 4 \amp 1 \cr 0 \amp 1 \amp 1 \amp 3 \cr \end{matrix}\right].
Thus A \left[\begin{matrix} 1 \cr 3 \cr 0 \cr \end{matrix}\right] = {\bf c}, so {\bf c}\in range(T).
